about: The course's 200 points (simulated: default_rng(11), class 0 around (0,0), class 1 around (2,2), unit spread). A sigmoid neuron trained by full-batch gradient descent, eta 0.5, from w = (0,0), b = 0; epochs[k] = [loss, accuracy, w1, w2, b] after k updates. The best threshold on x1 alone, and the line after 1000 epochs. lossGrid: mean cross-entropy over (w1, w2) at the final b, z[j*nx + i] at w1 = x[i], w2 = y[j]; path = (w1, w2, loss at the final b) per epoch. split: perceptron.py `_split` (150 train / 50 test, inputs standardised on the train rows).

bayes.why: log odds of two unit Gaussians at (0,0) and (2,2): 2 x1 + 2 x2 - 4

start.note: w = (0, 0), b = 0: every point scores 0.5, loss ln 2; accuracy counts p > 0.5

lossProfile.about: lossProfile: mean cross-entropy of the course's 200 points over (w1, w2), b profiled (set to its best) at each node, as T3's chi2 bowl profiles n_sig. z[j*nx + i] at w1 = x[i], w2 = y[j]; path[k] = [w1, w2, profiled loss, best b] at the weights after k updates (the logged training loss, epochs[k][0], lies on or above it). dk-landscape: src 'train-perceptron.json', key 'lossProfile', readout 'chi2' (with no chi2min the readout is the loss itself).

split.bandWhy: binomial sd at the mean accuracy for 50 test points, as the course draws it
